chapter: Retirement and the future of big bands
title: Correcting Babs Gonzalez's claim to have worked with Barnet
summary: Barnet says Lena Horne left in 1941 and Gonzalez never worked for him.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Damp, I think is the word.

In Valerie Wilmer's book, (Interruption in recording,) -- she says Babs Gonzalez's first name job was with Charlie Barnet in 1944. "He toured with alto saxophonist's big band for several weeks, but never recorded, mainly because

Lena Horne was then the featured attraction. Never one to pass up an opportunity for blowing his own metaphorical trumpet, Babs could not resist commenting, 'My job was more or less to help Lena out vocally. She's a great lady, but during that time I probably didn't hit the floor over seven times in maybe nine weeks, because I was down in the hall, rehearsing Lena'.
That's what it says in the book.

Well, that's strange because Lena Horne was with me in '40 and '41, and was long gone in '44, and while I've known his nibs Mr. Gonzalez for a long time he never worked for me. He's a very amusing guy, and he never toured with the band. To my knowledge he was never on my payroll for anything.
Okay. We took care of correcting that one.
